title: Application of 3D Ultrasound Imaging in School-based Screening for Scoliosis: A Prospective Cross-sectional Study
abstract: Abstract Purpose To investigate the feasibility and efficacy of 3D ultrasound imaging for large-scale school-based scoliosis screening Methods This cross-sectional study screened 9,128 students using a three-stage protocol: (1) Adams test with scoliometer (ATR > 5° as positive); (2) 3D ultrasound imaging with an ultrasound curvature angle (UCA) > 8° for referral and UCA ≥ 10°as the optimal diagnostic threshold via ROC analysis; and (3) whole-spine X-ray as the gold standard (Cobb angle ≥ 10°). Agreement between ultrasound and X-ray measurements was assessed using Bland-Altman analysis and Pearson correlation. Diagnostic performance was evaluated with confirmed scoliosis defined as a radiographic Cobb angle ≥ 10°. Results Among 132 positive initial screenings, 98 underwent ultrasound and 67 had confirmed scoliosis (screen-detected prevalence of 0.73%). Mean UCA was 12.53°±4.15° and Cobb angle was 13.55°±6.11°. Bland-Altman analysis showed a mean bias of -1.02° (95% LoA − 7.46° to 5.42°), with strong Pearson correlation (r = 0.91, p < 0.001; R² = 0.82). Among the 98 referred students, using UCA ≥ 10° as the threshold against X-ray-confirmed Cobb angle ≥ 10°, sensitivity was 89.5%, specificity 58.1%, accuracy 79.6%, PPV 82.2%, and NPV 72.0%. Conclusions This large population-based study confirms that 3D ultrasound serves as a feasible, radiation-free intermediate triage tool for school scoliosis screening. Our three-stage protocol preserves high sensitivity while cutting X-ray referrals by 25.8%. This tiered workflow minimizes unnecessary radiation exposure and optimizes healthcare resource use; refinements to referral thresholds and operator training may lower false-positive rates.

title: A Comprehensive Survey of Quantum and Quantum-Inspired Image Segmentation in the Context of Modern Segmentation Methods
abstract: Abstract Image segmentation remains one of the most extensively studied problems in computer vision, with applications ranging from medical image analysis and autonomous driving to remote sensing and industrial inspection. While deep learning approaches currently dominate the field, interest in quantum computing has motivated the development of quantum and quantum-inspired segmentation techniques that explore alternative strategies for image representation, optimization, and learning. This survey provides a comprehensive review of quantum and quantum-inspired image segmentation methods within the broader context of modern segmentation research. To establish this context, we first examine the evolution of image segmentation methodologies, covering classical image processing techniques, machine learning approaches, and contemporary deep learning architectures.We then organize the existing quantum image segmentation literature into four categories: quantum-inspired, tensor network-based, hybrid quantum-classical, and fully quantum methods. Across these categories, we analyze computational principles, image encoding and representation strategies, application domains, and datasets. We further compare quantum and quantum-inspired approaches with established segmentation paradigms in terms of supervision, scalability, and hardware requirements. Our analysis indicates that quantum-inspired methods currently represent the most developed direction, while hybrid approaches are emerging and fully quantum methods remain constrained by quantum hardware, data encoding costs, and scalability challenges. By connecting quantum image segmentation with the broader evolution of segmentation research, this survey provides a unified perspective on the field. It identifies current trends, open challenges, and promising future directions for researchers exploring the emerging role of quantum computing in image segmentation.

title: Computerized Tomography Based Evaluation of Morphometric and Angular Parameters of the Adult Femur among Kenyans
abstract: Abstract Background The femur and the pelvis are large weight bearing bones in the human body. The femur, the bone of the thigh region, is the longest and strongest bone. Anatomically, the femur is divided into proximal, mid and distal segments. The evaluation of the structural morphology of body structures using Computer Tomography (CT) scan enables 3-dimensional evaluation; study of both the external and internal anatomy of bones without necessitating their destruction and the evaluation of the relationship of bone structures with vital structures such as nerves and vessels. This radiological evaluation of the Femur would inform placement of intramedullary devices and safe surgical approaches for both open and minimally invasive surgeries. Objective To describe the radiological topography of the adult femur in Kenya. Methods A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted at Moi Teaching and Referral Hospital and St. Luke’s Orthopaedic and Trauma Hospital. Lower limb CT scan images from 120 participants of either sex aged at least 18 years were analysed. Three-dimensional reconstruction was performed using MATLAB 9.7, and measurements were analysed using STATA/MP 13.0. Morphometric and angular parameters were summarized using mean and corresponding standard deviation. Results Morphometric parameters of the femur revealed a mean anteroposterior (AP) width at the isthmus of 13.987 ± 2.265 mm and mediolateral (ML) width at the isthmus of 10.943 ± 2.598 mm. Angular parameters included a mean proximal diaphysis angle (PDA) of 8.871 ± 2.282° and distal diaphyseal angle of 9.358° (± 2.331). Conclusion The study provides key anatomical parameters of the femur and pelvis, which can inform the design of implants tailored for the local population. These findings also support improved surgical planning and fracture stabilization techniques.

title: Can simplified endoscopic score for Crohn’s disease be simpler? --Development and Validation of the Multimodal Activity Score for Crohn's Disease (MAS-CD)
abstract: Abstract Background Endoscopy is central to diagnosing and monitoring Crohn’s disease (CD), but current endoscopic scoring systems such as the Simplified Endoscopic Score for Crohn’s Disease (SES-CD) are complex, time-consuming, and limited when ileocolonoscopy is incomplete. Approximately 30–40% of CD patients cannot undergo full examinations, hindering comprehensive assessment. With mucosal healing now a key therapeutic target, there is an urgent need for a simpler, multimodal, and clinically practical scoring tool. Objectives To develop and prospectively validate a novel comprehensive assessment tool—the Multimodal Activity Score for Crohn’s Disease (MAS-CD)—that combines endoscopic and, when necessary, radiological parameters. Design: Multicenter development and prospective validation study. Methods Four parameters—ulcer size, ulcerated surface area, affected surface area, and stenosis severity—were scored on a 0–3 scale. For incomplete ileocolonoscopies, contrast-enhanced CT enterography (CTE) with optional magnetic resonance enterography (MRE) or intestinal ultrasound (IUS) were incorporated. Inter-rater reproducibility was assessed in 157 patients, and MAS-CD was developed using multivariable regression. Validation was conducted in an independent cohort of 91 patients. Correlations with SES-CD, Harvey-Bradshaw Index (HBI), serum C-reactive protein (CRP), albumin, and fecal calprotectin were analyzed. Results Interobserver agreement for MAS-CD parameters was substantial (Kappa 0.508–0.722; ICC = 0.888). MAS-CD strongly correlated with SES-CD (r = 0.816, p < 0.001) and showed significant associations with CRP (r = 0.28), HBI (r = 0.285), albumin (r=–0.208), and fecal calprotectin (r = 0.218) (all p < 0.05). MAS-CD differentiated remission from active disease, small bowel-from colonic-dominant phenotypes, and predicted treatment response more effectively than SES-CD (AUC 0.61 vs. 0.21, p < 0.05). Conclusion MAS-CD is a simplified, flexible, and reproducible multimodal scoring system that overcomes the limitations of incomplete endoscopic assessment. By integrating imaging data, it provides a clinically actionable tool for comprehensive disease activity monitoring and treat-to-target strategies in the biologic era.

title: Parasagittal High-Convexity Tightness Reveals a Focal Site of CSF Outflow Impairment in Ventriculomegaly
abstract: Abstract Introduction Disproportionately enlarged subarachnoid space hydrocephalus (DESH) and resistance to CSF outflow (R out ) are two of the most consistent diagnostic and prognostic markers in normal pressure hydrocephalus, yet it remains unclear whether they reflect a common pathophysiological process. A plausible link is that tightness of the high convexities adjacent to the superior sagittal sinus (SSS), the principal CSF outflow region, compromises CSF drainage and thereby increases R out . To test this hypothesis, we investigated the association between parasagittal high-convexity CSF volume near the SSS and R out in subjects undergoing MRI and CSF infusion testing. Methods We conducted a retrospective study of 621 individuals (581 with ventriculomegaly and 40 without), investigated with CSF infusion testing and brain MRI. Parasagittal high convexity CSF volumes were quantified using a semi-automated segmentation approach, focusing on anatomically defined high convexity regions. R out was derived from lumbar CSF infusion testing using standardised protocols. Associations between parasagittal CSF volume and R out were evaluated using correlation analyses, with additional assessment of demographic and structural confounders. Results An inverse relationship was observed between parasagittal high convexity CSF volume and R out (N = 621, Spearman Rho =-0.42, p < 0.001). This association was most pronounced when measurements were restricted to anatomically localised regions adjacent to the SSS, while more extended convexity regions demonstrated weaker relationships (N = 309, Rho=-0.14, p = 0.0002). The observed association was preserved after exclusion of healthy individuals. Age, sex, and ventricular volume did not significantly influence the relationship. Conclusions A localised relationship exists between parasagittal high-convexity morphology and resistance to CSF outflow. The regional specificity of this association suggests that DESH and R out may reflect a shared pathophysiological mechanism, which becomes apparent only when examined at anatomically strategic sites along the CSF outflow pathway.

title: Why Variance Metrics Cannot Validate ComBat Harmonization: Evidence from Three-Vendor Mammography Radiomics
abstract: Abstract ComBat is the standard method for removing scanner- and vendor-related variation from radiomic features, yet its success is conventionally judged by variance statistics (ICC, η², Kruskal-Wallis) that ComBat aligns by construction, making such validation nearly tautological. Using expert tumor segmentations from three mammography vendors (n=120; analysis subset n=91) and 59 standardized features, we tested ComBat with evidence independent of the moments it targets. After harmonization a linear classifier could no longer identify the vendor (AUC 0.56) but a leakage-free random forest identified it perfectly (AUC 1.00), and inter-vendor covariance structure persisted (0.259→0.244). Naive ComBat also erased a batch-correlated biological covariate, tumor size (p=4.0×10⁻⁸→0.10), which covariate-protected ComBat preserved. Variance-based reporting may therefore give false assurance of cross-vendor comparability. Harmonization adequacy should therefore be certified by independent non-linear separability rather than by the variance statistics ComBat directly targets.

title: Prognostic value of pretreatment sarcopenia in unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma treated with yttrium-90 radioembolization
abstract: Abstract Objective Sarcopenia is a prognostic biomarker in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but its impact after transarterial radioembolization (TARE) with yttrium-90 ( 90 Y) microspheres and its relationship with tumor absorbed dose remain unclear. We assessed the prognostic value of sarcopenia for local progression-free survival (LPFS), progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival (OS) in patients with HCC treated with TARE. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 75 patients with HCC treated with 90Y glass or resin microspheres between June 2022 and December 2024. Skeletal muscle index (SMI) was derived from the CT component of [ 18 F]fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography ([ 18 F]FDG PET/CT) at L3. Sarcopenia was defined using sex- and BMI-specific SMI cut-offs. Tumor absorbed dose was dichotomized at 485 Gy. Survival was assessed by Kaplan–Meier analysis, and prognostic factors were evaluated using Cox regression. Results Sarcopenia was present in 32 patients (42.7%). Compared with non-sarcopenic patients, sarcopenic patients had lower objective response (34.4% vs. 97.7%; p < 0.001) and disease control rates (62.5% vs. 100%; p < 0.001). Median LPFS, PFS, and OS were 6, 6, and 10 months in sarcopenic patients versus 21, 19 months, and not reached in non-sarcopenic patients (all p < 0.001). On multivariable analysis, sarcopenia independently predicted shorter LPFS (HR 4.0; 95% CI 2.1–7.7; p < 0.001), PFS (HR 2.8; 95% CI 1.6–5.2; p < 0.001), and OS (HR 5.5; 95% CI 2.5–12.0; p < 0.001). Tumor absorbed dose < 485 Gy independently predicted shorter LPFS (HR 1.9; 95% CI 1.1–3.6; p = 0.034), but not PFS (HR 1.7; 95% CI 0.94–3.0; p = 0.078) or OS (HR 1.7; 95% CI 0.81–3.6; p = 0.161). Conclusion Pretreatment sarcopenia is an independent predictor of LPFS, PFS, and OS after TARE for HCC. Tumor absorbed dose remains associated with local tumor control, but an adequate dose does not overcome the adverse prognosis associated with sarcopenia. Routine assessment of skeletal muscle mass may improve risk stratification and help identify patients requiring closer surveillance and earlier systemic therapy.

title: Ultrasound-Guided Paravertebral Nerve Block in Percutaneous Vertebroplasty: A Retrospective Analysis
abstract: Abstract Objective To retrospectively analyze the effectiveness of ultrasound-guided paravertebral nerve block in thoracolumbar fracture surgery. Methods Clinical data of 84 patients with thoracolumbar fractures who underwent percutaneous vertebroplasty at Xiaoshan District Traditional Chinese Medicine Hospital, Hangzhou, from July 2021 to July 2026 were retrospectively analyzed. Patients were divided into two groups based on the anesthesia method: the observation group (n = 42) received bilateral paravertebral nerve block combined with local anesthesia, while the control group (n = 42) received local anesthesia alone. The two groups were compared regarding intraoperative changes in heart rate (HR) and mean arterial pressure (MAP), Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) scores immediately post-surgery (T0), and at 6 hours (T1), 12 hours (T2), and 24 hours (T3) post-surgery, as well as postoperative complications and length of hospital stay. Results The retrospective study results indicated that, compared to the local anesthesia group, the paravertebral nerve block group had shorter operative time, more stable intraoperative MAP and HR, lower postoperative VAS scores, and shorter hospital stays.these differences were statistically significant (P < 0.05). No statistically significant difference was found in the incidence of postoperative complications between the two groups (P > 0.05). Conclusion Paravertebral nerve block anesthesia can stabilize intraoperative vital signs, shorten operative time, reduce postoperative pain scores, and demonstrates good safety.

title: Suspected Noninsulinoma Pancreatogenous Hypoglycemia Syndrome Following Truncal Vagotomy and Pyloroplasty: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Truncal vagotomy with pyloroplasty was historically a standard surgical treatment for refractory peptic ulcer disease (PUD) and PUD complicated by gastric outlet obstruction (GOO). Although these procedures are now infrequently performed, long-term metabolic complications may still occur. Noninsulinoma pancreatogenous hypoglycemia syndrome (NIPHS) is a rare cause of endogenous hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia, most commonly reported after bariatric surgery. Its occurrence following truncal vagotomy and pyloroplasty is exceptionally rare. Case Presentation A 46-year-old man presented with recurrent episodes of tremor, palpitations, diaphoresis, and difficulty concentrating occurring 3–4 hours after carbohydrate-rich meals. The symptoms began one year after truncal vagotomy and pyloroplasty performed for peptic ulcer disease complicated by gastric outlet obstruction and had progressively increased in frequency over the preceding six years. During symptomatic episodes, capillary blood glucose ranged from 47 to 53 mg/dL. Biochemical evaluation demonstrated endogenous hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia with inappropriately elevated insulin (12.5 µU/mL), C-peptide (4.38 nmol/L), and proinsulin (10.25 pmol/L), suppressed β-hydroxybutyrate (0.06 mmol/L), normal cortisol, and negative insulin autoantibodies. Abdominal MRI/MRCP revealed no evidence of insulinoma or other pancreatic lesions. In the absence of selective arterial calcium stimulation testing and pancreatic histopathology, a clinical diagnosis of NIPHS was made based on the characteristic postprandial presentation, biochemical findings, exclusion of insulinoma, and the patient's marked clinical improvement following dietary modification and acarbose. Conclusion NIPHS should be considered in the differential diagnosis of recurrent postprandial hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia in patients with a history of truncal vagotomy and pyloroplasty after insulinoma has been excluded. This case highlights an uncommon late complication of upper gastrointestinal surgery and emphasizes the importance of recognizing NIPHS even in resource-limited settings where advanced diagnostic investigations are unavailable.

title: Dual-encoder cross-scale dependency fusion network for placenta segmentation using MR and ultrasound images
abstract: Abstract Accurate placenta segmentation is essential for prenatal assessment, pregnancy management, and the diagnosis of placenta-related abnormalities. However, automatic placenta segmentation remains challenging due to complex anatomical structures, ambiguous boundaries, intensity variations, and substantial differences between imaging modalities. In this study, we propose a dual-encoder cross-scale dependency fusion network (DECSDF-Net) for placenta segmentation using MR and ultrasound images. The proposed DECSDF-Net adopts a dual-encoder architecture to extract complementary hierarchical features from two parallel encoding pathways. To enhance spatial representation, a cross-directional coordinate attention module (CDCAM) is introduced to capture directional dependencies and strengthen boundary-related features. Furthermore, a guided cross-scale dependency module (GCSDM) is designed to establish adaptive interactions among multi-level features, enabling effective information exchange between low-level spatial details and high-level semantic representations. An attention-guided enhanced receptive field block (AGERFB) is developed to improve contextual feature extraction by integrating multi-scale receptive fields with attention refinement. In addition, a progressive multi-scale feature fusion module (PMSFFM) is incorporated into the decoder to progressively aggregate features from different resolutions and enhance segmentation accuracy. To validate the effectiveness of DECSDF-Net, two placenta segmentation databases, namely Placenta-MR and Placenta-US, were constructed from magnetic resonance and ultrasound images. Compared with several state-of-the-art methods, DECSDF-Net achieved superior segmentation performance on both datasets. Specifically, the proposed method obtained Dice/MCC/Jaccard values of 0.8838/0.8775/0.7923 on Placenta-MR and 0.8778/0.8642/0.7826 on Placenta-US. Moreover, ablation studies confirmed the effectiveness of each designed module. These results demonstrate that DECSDF-Net provides accurate and robust placenta segmentation, showing promising potential for automated prenatal assessment and computer-aided diagnosis.

title: Eliminating False-Negative Discharges in Tuberculosis Screening: Multi-Cohort Development and Independent External Stress-Testing of an Auditable Conformal AI Safety Architecture
abstract: Abstract Background Deep learning tuberculosis triage risks silent false negatives from uncalibrated overconfidence, while benchmark AUROCs frequently reflect institutional artifacts. We evaluated an edge-deployable AI framework coupling DenseNet-121 with pre-analytic Input Quality Assurance (IQA), temperature scaling, Mondrian conformal prediction, and HiResCAM attribution. Methods We curated 12,599 radiographs across five institutions for development (training n=8,819, validation n=1,261, calibration n=1,261, test n=1,258), calibrating Mondrian bounds (α=0.05). The frozen 28.5 MB model was evaluated across 3,441 unseen external radiographs from rural secondary care (Solan, India; n=155), tertiary referral (NITRD New Delhi; n=278), and web-compressed imaging (Pakistan; n=3,008). Findings Across external Indian cohorts (n=433), the frozen model achieved AUROC 0.8613 (Solan rural CR, n=155; sensitivity 70.51%, specificity 87.01%) and AUROC 0.8721 (NITRD tertiary DR, n=278; sensitivity 78.40%, specificity 80.39%), pooling to AUROC 0.8682. On the internal test set (n=1,258, AUROC 0.9943), linear probe auditing revealed institutional acquisition shortcuts (Belarus cavitary TB vs RSNA normal controls, r=+0.7205). Noise retraining rescued Pakistan scans (AUROC 0.4982 to 0.7098) but degraded clean clinical scans (-0.20 AUROC drop). Crucially, while raw classifier sensitivities were 70.51% to 78.40%, assistive IQA and Mahalanobis interlocks eliminated autonomous false-negative discharges (0.00% autonomous discharge error, 0/203 active cases cleared without clinician review). Decision curve analysis demonstrated +14.07 net true positives per 1,000 cases and reduced unnecessary GeneXpert assays by 78.7%. The offline microservice operates with zero cloud cost, 348 MiB RAM, and 38.2 ms GPU latency (104 ms CPU). Interpretation Autonomous clearance is hazardous under sensor shift. By deferring indeterminate presentations to clinicians, conformal triage interlocks eliminate unreviewed false-negative discharges without feature distortion, providing a failsafe tool for resource-constrained clinics. Funding Independent departmental resources; no commercial funding.

title: Prognostic Value of PSMA Dominance on Dual-Tracer PET in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Prospective Single-Center Study
abstract: Abstract Background To evaluate the prognostic value of prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) findings in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and to assess its incremental prognostic value over fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) positron emission tomography (PET) and established clinical factors. Methods In this prospective, single-center study, 18 patients with HCC (mean age: 65.3±11.5years, 78%male) underwent dual-tracer PSMA and FDG PET imaging for staging (n=14) and restaging (n=4), with a median interval of 6 days between scans. Clinical variables, including age, gender, serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP), albumin-bilirubin (ALBI) grade, and Child-Pugh class, as well as imaging parameters derived from PSMA and FDG PET, were evaluated. Time to progression (TTP) and overall survival (OS) were assessed using the Kaplan–Meier method and compared with the log-rank test. Cox proportional hazards regression analysis was performed to identify independent predictors of survival. PSMA dominance was defined as PSMA-dominant uptake (PSMA>FDG). Results During a median follow-up of 15.5 months, 11 patients (61.1%) developed disease progression and 9 (50.0%) died. In Kaplan–Meier analysis, several clinical and imaging variables were associated with OS, including ascites, ALBI grade, Child-Pugh class, PSMA PET positivity, PSMA-detected extrahepatic disease (EHD), FDG-detected portal vein thrombosis (PVT), and PSMA dominance. For TTP, ascites, ALBI grade, Child-Pugh class, PSMA-detected EHD, and PVT detected on both PSMA and FDG were significant. In multivariable Cox analysis, PSMA dominance emerged as an independent predictor of OS (HR: 37.85, 95% CI:2.42-592.84, p = 0.010), together with Child-Pugh class (HR: 81.02, 95% CI:4.09-1603.51, p = 0.004) and AFP ≥200 ng/mL (HR: 13.86, 95% CI:1.41-135.91, p = 0.024). For TTP, ascites (HR: 48.82, 95% CI:X-Y, p = 0.004) and PSMA-detected EHD (HR: 16.28, 95% CI:X-Y, p = 0.024) remained independently associated with shorter TTP. Conclusion In HCC, disease progression appears to be primarily driven by tumor burden and extent, whereas overall survival is additionally influenced by liver function and tumor biology. Among PET-derived markers, PSMA dominance emerged as a potential imaging biomarker and was independently associated with overall survival, suggesting that the incremental prognostic value of PSMA PET may lie primarily in its ability to capture biologic heterogeneity beyond FDG PET alone.

title: A Longitudinal Study of Brain Volume Changes in Children With Growth Hormone Deficiency Treated With Recombinant Human Growth Hormone
abstract: Abstract Recombinant human growth hormone (rhGH) is the standard treatment for isolated growth hormone deficiency (IGHD), but its effects on structural brain development remain incompletely understood. This study evaluated the longitudinal volumetric changes in the pituitary gland and selected brain structures in children with IGHD following rhGH therapy. In this ambidirectional cohort study, 43 children with IGHD underwent MRI at baseline and after a mean follow-up of 1.6 ± 1.2 years following rhGH therapy, with age- and sex-matched controls recruited separately for baseline (n = 20) and follow-up (n = 21) evaluation. Pituitary volumes were manually segmented using 3D Slicer, while subcortical and corpus callosum structures were analysed using automated segmentation (Fastsurfer). At baseline, IGHD participants had significantly smaller pituitary and splenium volumes, while the remaining corpus callosum regions were larger compared with controls. Following rhGH therapy, pituitary and splenium volumes increased significantly (p < 0.01), with partial normalisation, while enlarged corpus callosum subregions showed significant volume reduction, indicating region-specific structural adaptation. rhGH therapy is therefore associated with region-specific brain volumetric changes and partial normalisation of structural abnormalities in children with IGHD, and MRI-based volumetry may serve as a useful biomarker for monitoring treatment-related brain structural changes.

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence for Opportunistic Osteoporosis Screening Using Lumbar Spine Imaging: Diagnostic Performance, Reproducibility, Effects of Few-Shot Prompting, and Comparison with Physicians
abstract: Abstract Purpose Osteoporosis remains underdiagnosed despite widespread availability of lumbar radiographs and computed tomography (CT). We compared physicians and multimodal generative artificial intelligence (AI) for opportunistic osteoporosis screening, focusing on diagnostic accuracy, reproducibility, and effects of few-shot prompting. Methods Forty-five lateral lumbar radiographs and 45 sagittal CT images were classified using DXA T-score thresholds of −1.0 and −2.5 as reference standards. Performance was compared among 42 board-certified orthopedic surgeons, 50 non-specialists, and ChatGPT, Gemini 3.1 Pro, and Claude 4 Opus. Each AI model evaluated all images five times under zero-shot and few-shot conditions, with 20 labeled reference cases provided for few-shot prompting. An exploratory analysis evaluated combined specialist-AI classifications using OR and AND rules. Results At the −1.0 cutoff, specialists outperformed non-specialists on radiographs (P<0.001). Claude achieved the highest radiographic accuracy (73.3%), followed by Gemini (64.4%), specialists (57.4%), ChatGPT (55.6%), and non-specialists (44.0%). Educational examples did not improve physician accuracy, and few-shot prompting did not consistently improve AI accuracy. However, reproducibility improved in several models, most notably Claude. An OR rule combining specialist and Claude classifications increased sensitivity to 80.0% on radiographs and 90.0% on CT, with reduced specificity. Conclusion Generative AI achieved physician-comparable performance under selected conditions but showed model-dependent variability. Few-shot prompting may improve consistency without improving accuracy. Exploratory combined assessment suggested complementary physician-AI errors may reduce missed cases at the cost of false-positive classifications. Generative AI may therefore serve as a decision-support tool for opportunistic osteoporosis screening but should complement rather than replace physician judgment.

title: Underlying histopathology features of white matter hyperintensities in vascular and neurodegenerative disorders: a systematic review
abstract: Abstract White matter hyperintensities (WMHs) are a hallmark of cerebral small vessel disease, commonly seen in cognitively normal older adults and patients with neurodegenerative disorders, and are thought to reflect varying degrees of tissue damage. Although FLAIR and T2-weighted MRI remain the best modalities for detecting WMHs, these lesions cannot be reliably distinguished macroscopically from normal appearing white matter, so standard neuropathology protocols do not specifically consider WMH regions unless MRI guidance is available. As a result, histopathological data on WMHs from gold-standard studies remain limited relative to their clinical prevalence. This review aimed to evaluate existing evidence linking MRI-defined WMHs to their underlying histopathology in postmortem brains from patients with various neurodegenerative disorders and aging controls. After a PubMed literature search and screening of abstracts and full texts, we included 45 articles: 10 on normal aging, 16 on Alzheimer's disease, 10 on vascular dementia, and 9 on related conditions. WMHs were histopathologically characterized by myelin loss (including spongiosis), axonal rarefaction, edema, dilated perivascular spaces, gliosis, arteriolosclerosis, and venous collagenosis, all indicative of underlying white matter pathology. The findings overall suggest that WMHs are pathologically heterogeneous, varying according to their anatomical location and distribution. Disease-specific differences in regional distribution, neuroinflammation, vascular pathology, and proteinopathy further contribute to their development and clinical significance, highlighting the need to consider both diagnosis and anatomical location when interpreting the pathological substrates of WMHs.

title: Development of Abdelwahab-Taha Stereotactic Software for Neurosurgery Surgical Planning
abstract: Abstract In frame-based stereotaxy, planning software must map image-derived coordinates into the physical coordinate system of the stereotactic frame, tightly coupling software design to hardware geometry. Most existing platforms are proprietary, cost-prohibitive, and hardware-restricted, limiting accessibility in resource-constrained settings. This study presents Abdelwahab–Taha Stereotactic (ATStereo) software, a source-available planning toolkit built as a 3D Slicer extension and tailored to the geometric configuration of the Abdelwahab stereotactic frame. ATStereo features real-time fiducial visualization, 3D frame kinematic reconstruction anchored to dual physically accessible reference origins, and bilateral trajectory planning integrated with the DISTAL subcortical atlas. Spatial alignment accuracy and workflow duration were evaluated on phantom computed tomography datasets across five operators (three novices, two experts). Mean registration root mean square error was 0.40 ± 0.15 mm (range 0.12–0.94 mm), remaining strictly below a 1.0 mm quality-control threshold. Mean workflow time was 1.86 ± 0.53 min, with novice performance stabilizing within 5–10 trials. Bilateral trajectory planning on clinical Parkinson's disease deep brain stimulation datasets achieved 100% anatomical safety clearance and sub-millimeter agreement with implanted electrode positions (0.256 ± 0.072 mm). Compared with BrainStereo, ATStereo showed lower maximum registration error and an approximate threefold reduction in workflow time.

title: Deep Transfer Learning for Automated Cervical Cell-Type Classification in Pap-Smear Images: A Comparative and Explainable Study
abstract: Abstract Automated interpretation of cervical cytology images has been an active area of research for enabling large scale, reproducible screening workflows. Although deep learning approaches have been remarkably successful at many medical image classification tasks, classifying the five different cervical cell types remains a challenge since several classes have spectrally similar nuclear textures, cytoplasmic textures, and structures. Here we implement a comparative transfer learning approach to classify five different cytomorphology’s: dyskeratotic, koilocytotic, metaplastic, parabasal, and superficial-intermediate from an image collection curated for experiments to consist of 5015 usable images separated into a stratified training validation and independent test set of 3509/753/753 images 3509/753/753, respectively. We trained three ImageNet-pretrained convolutional neural network architectures (ResNet50DenseNet111EfficientNet B0) with a common approach consisting of data augmentation, class weighted training, frozen-backbone training, and fine-tuning. The architectures were assessed for accuracy, macro-precision, macro-recall, macro-F1, weighted F1, class-wise sensitivity and specificity and one-vs-rest macro-ROC-AUC scores. ResNet50 achieved the best class-wise scores across the architectures on the held-out test set with 91.50% accuracy, 91.72% macro-precision, 91.82% macro-recall, 91.76% macro-F1, 91.48% weighted F1 and 99.12% macro-ROC-AUC. Out of 753 classifications on the test set images, 689 classifications were accurate and 64 images were misclassified by the neural network. Class-wise analysis of sensitivities and specificities highlighted the performance of the network had an excellent distinction between Parabasal and Superficial-Intermediate classes, but a more difficulties classifying the Koilocytotic and Metaplastic classes. Directly analysing the CNN model, the locations of the input in the images which contributed the most to the classification was identified using Grad-CAM. Bottom line, transfer learning can be excellent when applying neural networks to cervical cytological cell classification, but further thorough validation would be necessary in the clinical setting.

title: AI-Assisted Mammography Screening: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Cancer Detection, Recall Rates and Workflow Outcomes
abstract: Abstract Structured Abstract Background Breast cancer is the most commonly diagnosed cancer in women worldwide. Organised mammography screening reduces mortality by approximately 20 to 40 percent, yet conventional double reading is labour intensive and subject to inter-reader variability. Artificial intelligence systems based on deep learning have been introduced into screening pathways as concurrent readers, triage tools or second readers. A synthesis of recent programme level evidence is needed to guide implementation decisions. Objective To systematically review and summarise the effects of AI assisted mammography screening on cancer detection rate, recall rate, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value and radiologist workload relative to standard double reading, focusing on studies published from 2021 onward. Methods This systematic review and meta-analysis followed PRISMA 2020. A protocol was prepared a priori. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched from 1 January 2021 to 23 August 2026. Titles, abstracts, full texts, and data extraction were performed independently by two reviewers in duplicate, with discrepancies resolved by consensus. Results Twelve studies including 1 138 504 screening examinations were retained. The PRAIM prospective implementation study in Germany (463 094 women) reported a cancer detection rate of 6.7 per 1000 with AI support versus 5.7 per 1000 without, a relative increase of 17.6 percent, while recall remained non inferior (37.4 versus 38.3 per 1000). The MASAI randomised trial in Sweden demonstrated higher detection (6.4 versus 5.0 per 1000), a 44 percent reduction in screen reading volume and non inferior interval cancer rates. Triage configurations consistently lowered recall and workload. Pooled absolute gain in cancer detection was approximately 0.7 to 0.9 cancers per 1000 screens. Sensitivity improved and specificity was preserved in concurrent and triage deployments. title: Extent of Resection as the Primary Independent Predictor of Progression- Free Survival in Atypical Intracranial Meningioma: A Retrospective Single- Center Study of 187 Patients
abstract: Abstract Purpose Atypical meningiomas (WHO grade 2) show considerable biological heterogeneity and substantial recurrence rates despite surgical treatment, while reliable prognostic markers remain limited. We aimed to identify clinical and radiographic predictors of progression-free survival (PFS) in a large single-center cohort. Methods We retrospectively analysed 187 patients with histopathologically confirmed atypical intracranial meningioma (2016–2023), categorised by extent of resection (gross total resection [GTR] vs subtotal resection [STR]) and treatment strategy (surgery alone vs surgery plus radiotherapy). Kaplan–Meier and univariate/multivariate Cox regression were applied to identify predictors of PFS. Results GTR was achieved in 168 patients (89.8%) and STR in 19 (10.2%); tumor progression or recurrence occurred in 25 patients (13.4%). On multivariate analysis, extent of resection was the only independent predictor of shortened PFS (adjusted HR 3.09, 95% CI 1.14–8.37; p = 0.026). Peritumoral edema showed a consistent, non-significant trend toward shortened PFS (adjusted HR 2.43, 95% CI 0.92–6.37; p = 0.072). Age (HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.37–1.92; p = 0.7) and radiotherapy (HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.43–2.26; p > 0.9) were not significantly associated with PFS. Edema was not associated with the extent of resection or radiotherapy administration. Conclusion Extent of resection is the strongest independent predictor of PFS in atypical intracranial meningioma, reaffirming maximal safe resection as the central surgical objective. Peritumoral edema showed a consistent but non-significant trend that warrants confirmation in larger, adequately powered multicenter cohorts.

title: The Role of Bronchoscopy pada Acute Lung Atelectasis Due to Airway Mucus Plugging: A Case report
abstract: Abstract Background: Acute lung atelectasis caused by airway mucus plugging is a potentially reversible cause of respiratory failure, particularly in postoperative and critically ill patients. Prompt recognition and timely intervention are essential to prevent prolonged hypoxemia, mechanical ventilation, and other serious complications. Flexible bronchoscopy is considered the gold standard for diagnosing and treating obstructive atelectasis by directly identifying and removing airway obstruction. Case Presentation: A 32-year-old man developed severe hypoxemia and complete right lung atelectasis on the second day following exploratory laparotomy for abdominal trauma. Despite chest tube insertion, invasive mechanical ventilation, and supportive management, oxygenation remained critically impaired. Bedside lung ultrasonography demonstrated extensive right lung collapse. Therapeutic flexible bronchoscopy revealed complete obstruction of the right upper lobe bronchus by a thick mucus plug, with additional retained secretions in the right bronchial tree. Bronchial toilet and suctioning successfully restored airway patency. Immediate post-procedure chest radiography demonstrated significant right lung re-expansion, while arterial oxygenation improved markedly, with PaO₂ increasing from 40 mmHg to 194 mmHg. The patient was subsequently weaned from mechanical ventilation, experienced progressive clinical recovery, and was discharged from the intensive care unit in stable condition. Conclusion: This case highlights that mucus plug-induced atelectasis should be considered in postoperative patients presenting with sudden hypoxemia and radiographic evidence of lung collapse. Early therapeutic flexible bronchoscopy provides both definitive diagnosis and effective treatment by restoring airway patency, promoting rapid lung re-expansion, improving oxygenation, facilitating ventilator weaning, and optimizing clinical outcomes when conservative management is unsuccessful.

title: An ablation measured twice: small component effects can change sign across repeated training runs in breast-cancer histopathology segmentation
abstract: Abstract Purpose. An ablation table reports what each component contributes. We ask whether those contributions reproduce: measure run-to-run variability, run a seven-configuration ablation, then repeat it. Methods. On BCSS under an institution-held-out protocol (5273/1087/2256 patches, no slide or site shared), one configuration trained twice at each of twelve seeds gave a mean absolute paired difference R = 0.0081 Dice. A seven-configuration ablation of stain processing, multi-scale features and cross-scale attention ran at three seeds per cell, then repeated. Contrasts use paired bootstrap and Wilcoxon tests, Holm corrected, over 1563 tumour-bearing patches, resampling slides. Results. Contrast displacement between measurements averaged 0.0046 Dice and varied 4.6-fold, against 27-fold variation in first-measurement contrast magnitude. What a contrast retained fell away with its size: the three largest kept sign, significance and 59–87% of their magnitude; stain processing kept its sign and 13%; the three smallest were no larger than the displacement and two changed sign. Cross-scale attention measured −0.0035, −0.0008, −0.0043, then +0.0022, +0.0040, −0.0058. Conclusion. In this experiment, contrasts comparable in magnitude to the observed re-run displacement were not directionally stable, motivating replication before component-level interpretation.

title: Emphysematous Osteomyelitis of the Lumbar Spine Masked by a Urinary Tract Infection in a Diabetic Patient: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background: Emphysematous osteomyelitis (EO) is a rare and aggressive gas-forming bone infection, most commonly affecting diabetic or immunocompromised patients, with the vertebrae, pelvis, and femur being frequently involved sites. It is most often caused by Klebsiella pneumoniae or Escherichia coli via hematogenous spread, and because of its rarity, its diagnosis is frequently overlooked. Case Presentation: We report the case of a 50-year-old diabetic and hypertensive female who presented with dysuria and dull lower back pain, initially managed as a routine UTI with antibiotics and adjustment of her diabetic regimen. When her urinary symptoms failed to resolve, contrast-enhanced CT of the kidneys, ureters, and bladder incidentally revealed emphysematous osteomyelitis of the L3-L4 vertebrae, with urine culture growing Klebsiella species. Despite targeted intravenous antibiotic therapy (meropenem), her clinical response was poor, necessitating anterior corpectomy with cage reconstruction. Her postoperative course was complicated by severe pain and poorly controlled diabetes, and she subsequently died of cardiopulmonary arrest. Conclusion: This case underscores the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for emphysematous osteomyelitis in diabetic patients presenting with back pain, as delayed diagnosis in an immunocompromised host can culminate in a fatal outcome despite aggressive medical and surgical management.

title: Automated Brachial Plexus Localization in Ultrasound Using Lightweight Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: Abstract Purpose: Accurate localization of the brachial plexus in ultrasound images is critical for regional anesthesia and perioperative care. Traditional manual interpretation is time-consuming and operator-dependent, while segmentation-based deep learning models, though precise, often demand substantial computational resources, limiting deployment in resource-constrained settings. This study evaluated lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures for automated classification of brachial plexus nerve location into four anatomical quadrants, balancing predictive performance with computational efficiency for point-of-care (POC) environments. Methods: B-mode ultrasound images from the Kaggle Ultrasound Nerve Segmentation dataset were transformed from segmentation masks into a five-class classification task. Three CNN backbones—ResNet34, MobileNetV2, and EfficientNetB0—were trained using 3-fold cross-validation. Data augmentation and class-balancing strategies were applied. Model performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, confusion matrices, and pairwise statistical testing. Results All three models achieved comparable overall performance, with mean accuracies ranging from 0.7288 to 0.7320 and macro-averaged F1-scores from 0.7333 to 0.7365. ResNet34 had the highest mean accuracy and F1-score, though differences between architectures were not statistically significant. Per-class analysis revealed strong performance for majority classes (0 and 2) and lower precision and F1-scores for minority classes, particularly class 3. MobileNetV2 and EfficientNetB0 demonstrated high computational efficiency suitable for on-device deployment. Conclusion Lightweight CNN backbones provide reliable performance for brachial plexus quadrant classification in ultrasound images. While ResNet34 offered marginally higher accuracy, MobileNetV2 and EfficientNetB0 provided better suitability for POC deployment due to lower computational requirements. Future work should address class imbalance and expand evaluation to larger, more diverse datasets.

title: A tunable Synthetic Vascularized Eye Fundus for patient-free retinal imaging validation
abstract: Abstract The validation of novel retinal imaging techniques and motion-correction algorithms is often constrained by biological variability and the lack of ground-truth data in \textit{in vivo} measurements. To address this limitation, patient-free validation platforms require standardized targets that mimic selected optical and structural properties of the human eye. Here, we present a Synthetic Vascularized Eye Fundus (SVEF), a perfusable and contrast-tunable microfluidic insert designed for ophthalmic eye phantom platforms. The SVEF features a high-density, retinal-like vascular network fabricated by soft lithography using a custom polydimethylsiloxane-zinc oxide (PDMS--ZnO) composite. This substrate acts as a bright, diffusely scattering background, while perfusion with hemoglobin solutions generates physiologically relevant absorbing vessel-like structures. By optimizing the hemoglobin concentration, we achieved a vessel-to-background contrast closely matching that of \textit{in vivo} human fundus images. We validated the SVEF as a robust structural reference for image registration, demonstrating accurate retrieval of imposed saccade-like micro-displacements and enabling the enhancement of multi-frame fluorescence imaging. Finally, we confirmed the compatibility of the device with biological assays by successfully integrating and imaging human iPSC-derived retinal neurons. The SVEF provides a reproducible, patient-free environment for benchmarking ophthalmoscopic systems, optimizing image-registration pipelines and supporting versatile \textit{in vitro} retinal experiments.

title: A Resource-Constrained Evaluation of Fine-Tuned Deep Learning and Local Zero-Shot Vision-Language Models for Brain MRI Slice Classification
abstract: Abstract Fine-tuned deep learning (DL) classifiers report near-saturated performance on public brain MRI slice datasets, but dataset leakage, lack of patient-level metadata, and limited robustness evaluation restrict their interpretation. Concurrently, multimodal large language models (MLLMs) enable zero-shot image understanding, yet their unadapted zero-shot performance under local hardware constraints remains unverified. We conducted a paired evaluation comparing fine-tuned DL architectures (ResNet18, EfficientNet-B0, ConvNeXt-Tiny, ViT-B/16) across three seeds against local zero-shot MLLMs (Qwen3-VL-2B/8B, MedGemma-4B) on a locked, leakage-screened 260-image four-class evaluation set using a single NVIDIA RTX 3080 GPU (10 GB). We evaluated ImageNet pretraining on ResNet18, executed a 35,100-inference controlled corruption matrix across five synthetic transformations, and compiled a frozen 24-case Grad-CAM failure gallery. Fine-tuned ConvNeXt-Tiny achieved the highest mean Macro-F1 (0.9610 ± 0.0041), followed by EfficientNet-B0 (0.9531 ± 0.0069), pretrained ResNet18 (0.9476 ± 0.0024), and ViT-B/16 (0.9284 ± 0.0157). ImageNet pretraining exceeded scratch training by +0.0617 Macro-F1 (95% CI [0.0077, 0.1192]; scratch seed SD 0.0515), though scratch models exhibited marked seed-level initialization sensitivity. The strongest local zero-shot MLLM (Qwen3-VL-8B) reached Macro-F1 0.3991, yielding a large observed performance gap under the tested zero-shot, label-only setting (McNemar p < 0.001). Under corruptions, ConvNeXt-Tiny had the numerically lowest mean Macro-F1 drop (0.0253). Grad-CAM maps revealed spatial shifts during perturbation failures, though focal maps were also observed in misclassified cases. Under constrained local compute, which restricts deployable model parameter scale, the tested fine-tuned DL models substantially outperformed the unadapted zero-shot MLLMs evaluated without task-specific fine-tuning on this slice-level benchmark. High in-domain scores must be interpreted conservatively alongside dataset provenance, corruption sensitivity, and post-hoc explanation limits.

title: Relative contributions of reconstruction pipeline and MRI field strength to hippocampal shape variation
abstract: Abstract Objective Ultra-high-field 7T MRI provides increased signal-to-noise ratio and spatial resolution compared with 3T MRI, but contributions of field strength and reconstruction methodology to whole-hippocampus shape remain incompletely characterized. We evaluated their relative contributions to hippocampal shape variation. Materials and Methods MRI data were acquired from ten healthy adults scanned at 3T and 7T in a within-subject design. Right hippocampal 3D models were reconstructed using FSL, FreeSurfer, HippUnfold, and manual segmentation. Shape was quantified using geometric morphometrics based on 97 landmarks and semilandmarks. Procrustes ANOVA assessed effects of subject, reconstruction pipeline, and field strength. Results Subject was the principal source of hippocampal shape variation ( R² =0.194, P < 0.0001), followed by reconstruction pipeline ( R² =0.050, P = 0.0003) and field strength ( R² =0.025, P < 0.0001). Field strength and reconstruction pipeline interacted significantly ( R² =0.045, P = 0.0022). Hippocampal size showed significant agreement between field strengths ( r = 0.741, P < 0.0001), whereas shape correspondence was weaker but significant ( r = 0.371, P < 0.0001). FSL showed the smallest within-subject 3T–7T shape differences and closest agreement with manual segmentation. Discussion In this pilot cohort, reconstruction methodology had greater influence than field strength. Field-strength-related differences were modest relative to inter-individual and methodological effects, supporting whole-hippocampus morphometric analyses using 3T MRI under the evaluated imaging conditions.

title: Baseline Musculoskeletal Imaging Abnormalities and Subsequent Injury in Asymptomatic Athletes: A Systematic Review and Exploratory Meta-Analysis
abstract: Abstract Purpose To determine whether abnormal baseline magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or diagnostic ultrasound in athletes asymptomatic in the imaged region predicts subsequent same-region symptomatic injury. Methods A multi-database literature search was screened against prespecified criteria. Eligible studies imaged asymptomatic athletes before longitudinal clinical follow-up and reported an abnormal-imaging denominator. Risk of bias used the Quality In Prognosis Studies framework. Achilles and patellar tendon risk ratios (RRs) were pooled separately using exploratory DerSimonian–Laird random-effects models. Results Of 979 screened records, 78 reports were sought, 61 were assessed, and 16 reports representing 11 cohorts were included; four reports contributed six structure-specific estimates. In collegiate athletes, abnormal imaging predicted time-loss injury of the patellar tendon (adjusted RR 10.7, 95% confidence interval [CI] 4.1–27.8), Achilles tendon (adjusted RR 19.2, 95% CI 6.6–55.7), and plantar fascia (adjusted RR 13.3, 95% CI 1.4–104.8). Pooled RRs were 5.43 (95% CI 1.28–23.13; I²=81.1%) for Achilles outcomes and 3.15 (95% CI 1.11–8.94; I²=83.4%) for patellar outcomes. Youth medial-elbow abnormality also predicted injury (17/59 vs 18/151; crude RR 2.42, 95% CI 1.36–4.31). MRI findings were less consistent. Conclusion Baseline imaging abnormalities identify higher-risk groups, most consistently on Achilles and patellar tendon ultrasound, but prediction is heterogeneous and many abnormal structures remain asymptomatic. Imaging should inform monitoring and contextual load management, not serve alone as an indication for restriction or invasive treatment.

title: Renal Vascular Complications Requiring Embolization After Partial Nephrectomy: A Systematic Review and Exploratory Meta-analysis
abstract: Abstract Purpose To estimate transarterial embolization (TAE) incidence after partial nephrectomy and evaluate surgical-approach associations and treatment outcomes. Methods A sensitive literature search across PubMed, CINAHL, and Google Scholar yielded 506 records that underwent manual screening and extraction. Eligible cohorts required identifiable denominators and exact postoperative TAE counts; informative abstracts were eligible. Search dates and complete strategies were unavailable. Patient-denominator proportions and unadjusted within-study risk ratios were pooled using restricted maximum likelihood and modified Hartung–Knapp intervals. Risk of bias used an adapted six-domain framework. Results Fifty-four reports were retained: 28 full texts and 26 abstract-only reports. The primary synthesis comprised 52 patient-denominator cohorts, 420 TAE patients, and 17,831 reported patient denominators. Pooled incidence was 2.70% (95% confidence interval 2.23–3.28%; I² = 64.0%); full-text-only incidence was 2.93% (2.19–3.92%). Two procedure-denominator reports were excluded from the primary pool. Robotic versus open, robotic versus laparoscopic, and laparoscopic versus open risk ratios were 0.55 (0.11–2.65), 0.34 (0.06–1.85), and 1.92 (0.84–4.40), respectively. Embolization frequently achieved reported hemostasis, sometimes after repeat treatment; renal functional findings varied. Conclusion Approximately 3% underwent TAE in reported cohorts, with substantial heterogeneity and no established surgical-approach superiority. Abstract-only evidence, surveillance differences, and possible cohort overlap limit certainty. Radiologists should distinguish imaging-detected lesions from treatment-requiring events and interpret embolization risk alongside clinical presentation and surveillance practices.

title: End-to-End Agentic AI Framework for Cross-Dataset Medical Image Classification Using CNNs, Vision Transformers, Explainable AI, Robustness Analysis, and LLM-Driven Clinical Reporting
abstract: Abstract Medical image classification requires more than high predictive accuracy. A practically useful artificial intelligence system must also provide reliable confidence estimates, robust-ness under image perturbations, interpretable predictions, and meaningful reporting for downstream decision support. This project presents an end-to-end comparative medical imaging framework that evaluates Convolutional Neural Networks and Vision Transformers across three heterogeneous medical imaging tasks: Chest X-Ray pneumonia classification, Brain MRI tumor detection, and dermoscopic Skin Cancer classification. The evaluated architectures include ResNet50, EfficientNet-B0, DenseNet121, DeiT-Small, and Swin-Tiny. The framework integrates transfer learning, class-imbalance handling, model calibration, bootstrap confidence intervals, robustness evaluation, failure-case analysis, Grad-CAM explainability, ensemble learning , and extensive performance metrics. In addition, an LLM-driven reporting component is incorporated to generate structured model-comparison summaries, explainability interpretations, and decision-support reports. The LLM layer is constrained to provide research-oriented assistance rather than autonomous clinical diagnosis. Experimental results demonstrate that CNN architectures remain highly effective for structured radiographic images, while Vision Transformers provide strong performance and robustness for more contextually complex Brain MRI and dermoscopic imaging tasks.

title: Clinical Efficacy of Multiparametric Magnetic Resonance Imaging and Proton Spectroscopy in the Evaluation of Complex Ring-Enhancing Intracranial Lesions: A Four-Case Series from Pacific International Hospital, Papua New Guinea
abstract: Abstract Background: Ring-enhancing lesions (RELs) remain a persistent diagnostic challenge in neuroradiology, as neoplastic, infectious, and granulomatous processes frequently overlap in their conventional MRI appearance. Accurate differentiation is critical for guiding management, particularly in resource-limited settings such as Papua New Guinea (PNG), where access to advanced neuroimaging is concentrated in a few centers and specialist manpower is limited. Study setting and design: This retrospective case series was conducted at Pacific International Hospital (PIH), Port Moresby, PNG, over four months (June–September 2026). Four brain MRI cases were included: three presenting as ring-enhancing masses, and one miscellaneous nerve sheath tumour at the craniocervical junction and C1–C2 level. Materials and methods: Of the four cases, two were referred from Port Moresby General Hospital and two were managed in-house at PIH. Conventional MRI sequences, supplemented by single-voxel MR spectroscopy (MRS) in selected cases, were used to evaluate metabolite profiles and to help differentiate primary brain tumour, metastatic disease, and infective processes such as tuberculoma. Results: One case, an 18-year-old male, demonstrated a cortical high-grade glioma with elevated choline-to-N-acetylaspartate (Cho/NAA >1.5) and choline-to-creatine (Cho/Cr >2) ratios, favouring a glial neoplasm despite an atypical age. A second case, a 29-year-old male with constitutional symptoms, showed multifocal ring-enhancing lesions with a preserved NAA peak and Cho/NAA <1, consistent with CNS tuberculoma and correlating with the clinical history. A third case demonstrated periventricular, splenial, and parieto-occipital rim-enhancing and serpentine lesions, radiologically indistinguishable between tuberculoma and neurosarcoidosis; tuberculoma was favoured on supporting clinical evidence. A fourth, miscellaneous case demonstrated a craniocervical/C1–C2 nerve sheath tumour with a characteristic dumbbell configuration on T2-FLAIR and post-contrast T1-weighted imaging. Conclusion: This first PNG-based series demonstrates the added diagnostic value of MRS in characterising ring-enhancing lesions and illustrates how strengthened referral pathways from provincial and district-level facilities to centres equipped with advanced imaging can accelerate diagnosis and improve management outcomes.

title: Probabilistic three-dimensional mineralogical characterisation of drill core using μXRF and XCT: application to the Nautanen North IOCG deposit
abstract: Abstract Accurate mineralogical characterisation of drill cores is important for quantifying variability and supporting geometallurgical interpretations. Conventional assays provide bulk elemental concentrations but do not preserve mineral distributions, whereas individual non-destructive methods provide only partial mineralogical information. In this study, a probabilistic integrated framework was developed for three-dimensional mineralogical mapping, using four drill-core samples from Nautanen North, northern Sweden, as a case study. Micro-X-ray fluorescence (µXRF) maps classified with the Advanced Mineral Identification and Characterization System (AMICS) were co-registered with corresponding X-ray computed tomography (XCT) surfaces to derive mineralogical labels, which were used as two-dimensional supervision for a deep learning segmentation model, with XCT responses as the input. Detailed mineralogy was consolidated into four XCT-supported classes: Matrix silicates, Quartz, Garnet and Fe-bearing sulphides and oxides. Generalisation was evaluated using nested leave-one-sample-out validation, and predicted class probabilities were calibrated to better reflect prediction reliability. The selected support-aware calibrated ensemble achieved a mean accuracy of 0.899 and a mean macro Dice coefficient of 0.583. Matrix silicates transferred most consistently, whereas the Fe-bearing sulphides and oxides class remained difficult to discriminate because of its heterogeneous and overlapping XCT responses. The calibrated ensemble was subsequently applied to predict the mineralogical classes within a half-core XCT volume. Predictions remained spatially coherent across the evaluated XCT volume, with high confidence, low normalised predictive entropy and high spatial agreement. The framework demonstrates the potential to extend targeted surface mineralogical observations into three-dimensional predictions of mineralogical classes, accompanied by class probabilities and uncertainty fields, that can support geometallurgical domain definition and the selection of suitable samples for additional mineralogical analysis or metallurgical testing.

title: Evaluation Metrics for Image Classification, Segmentation and Localization
abstract: Abstract Evaluation metrics dictate the incentives for an image analysis system, detect remaining failures, and verify any proposed improvement in scientific or clinical claims. Despite the mathematical similarity of classification, segmentation, and localization, the units, matching criteria, and practice implications vary across these tasks. The current review analyzes the distinctions through the lens of a selected sample of 150 bibliographically validated references, including 10 papers from the provided author profile. It incorporates foundational statistics, state-of-the-art benchmarking practices, medical imaging use cases, and recent developments in uncertainties, selective prediction, and deployment. The review organizes 72 metrics and corresponding evaluation quantities by the question they answer: correctness of decision, score discrimination, reliability of probabilities, spatial correspondence, recovery of objects, localization of geometry, or practical utility. Comparisons describe equations, assumptions, aggregation approaches, advantages, and failures. Ten deterministic worked examples demonstrate prevalence effects, constant discrimination and worsening probability scores, reverse rankings because of aggregation, hidden border failures by overlap, detection matching, physical landmark errors, and the cost of abstaining. Twenty-four numeric instances from 4 separate publications supply additional citations and examples without pooling the inconsistent results. The primary takeaway is that a sound evaluation requires a small and preselected set of metrics, complementary to each other, applicable to the defined population, unit, reference standard, and decision. For classification, operating point performance is always required, along with discrimination and probability metrics. Segmentation demands appropriate measures of overlap, borders, and object topology. Localization needs explicitly stated criteria of correspondence and tolerance and false positive control. Independent partitioning, uncertainties, subgroups, and workflow outputs determine the interpretability of the metrics. This manuscript is an organized critical review and methodology resource, but not a completed systematic review according to PRISMA criteria, meta-analysis, or benchmark of a new model. The attached list of metrics, reference export, extraction notes, computational code, and reporting checklist help design and validate reproducible studies and author reviews.

title: Brain Tumor Segmentation in the Foundation-Model
abstract: Abstract Automated brain tumor segmentation has progressed from handcrafted pipelines and U-Net variants to self-configuring 3D CNNs, transformer hybrids, state-space models, diffusion based segmenters, promptable models and brain-specific foundation models. Yet the field’s central scientific problem has changed: another fractional gain in Dice on a familiar BraTS split provides limited evidence that a system will remain reliable when MRI sequences are missing, scanners and institutions change, lesions are small or multifocal, postoperative anatomy is distorted, or uncertainty is high. This structured critical review synthesizes 150 references with emphasis on 2025–2026 and compares architectures, multimodal fusion strategies, preprocessing, missing-modality learning, self-supervision, foundation-model adaptation, federated learning, domain adaptation, uncertainty quantification and clinical translation. We organize evidence around adult glioma, pediatric tumors, brain metastases, meningioma and longitudinal/postoperative applications; distinguish region overlap from lesion detection and volumetric clinical endpoints; and critically examine leakage, site confounding, hidden test reuse, pretraining contamination, annotation uncertainty and challenge-overfitting. Recent evidence is especially informative: brain MRI foundation models such as BrainIAC and BrainFound improve label efficiency and cross-task transfer, while task specific systems such as nnU-Net and carefully engineered 2.5D/3D networks remain formidable full-data baselines. Missing-modality studies increasingly favor adaptive fusion, distillation and modality dropout over naive zero-filling; uncertainty work is moving toward conformal and evidential approaches that can identify cases requiring expert review; and external studies of metastases and meningiomas demonstrate why lesion-wise, site-stratified and human-in-the-loop evaluation is essential. We propose DATA-SEG, Dataset, Annotation, Train/test integrity, Architecture, Statistics, External robustness and Governance, as a reporting and evaluation framework. The review concludes that the next high-impact phase of brain tumor segmentation should prioritize post-cutoff hidden benchmarks, cross-site robustness, missing-sequence stress tests, calibrated selective segmentation, multi-rater probabilistic ground truth and longitudinal clinical readouts rather than leaderboard optimization alone.

title: Comparison of clinical and pathological characteristics between localized giant cell and fibroadenoma of tendon sheath
abstract: Abstract Objective: To explore the clinical and pathological characteristics of localized giant cell tumor of tendon sheath (L-GCTS) and fibroma of tendon sheath (FTS), and to compare and analyze them. Methods: 241 cases of L-GCTS and 41 cases of FTS who underwent surgical resection and diagnosis at Wuxi Ninth People's Hospital from 2019 to 2023 were collected. Clinical and pathological data of all cases were organized for retrospective analysis. Chi-square test was used to analyze differences between groups. Results: Comparing our two groups of cases, we found that L-GCTS is more common, while FTS is less common. However, the two were very similar in clinical features, disease course, age of onset, tumor size and overall appearance, as well as imaging manifestations; In our case, L-GCTS was more common in female patients, and there was no significant gender difference in FTS; L-GCTS was more common in the right hand, FTS was also more common in the hand, but the left incidence rate is slightly higher than the right, with no significant difference; In addition, a small number of L-GCTS were accompanied by damage to surrounding tissues, and 41 cases of FTS did not cause damage to surrounding tissues; L-GCTS and FTS are mostly single lesions, with a few being multiple lesions; Among 241 cases of L-GCTS, 235 were primary cases, 6 were recurrent cases, and 41 cases of FTS were all primary cases; The coincidence rate between preoperative imaging diagnosis and postoperative pathological diagnosis of L-GCTS was 89%, and the coincidence rate between preoperative imaging diagnosis and postoperative pathological diagnosis of FTS was 55.3%. The main reason was that it is easier to misdiagnose FTS as L-GCTS before surgery; There were certain differences in pathological and immunohistochemical manifestations between the two. Conclusion: L-GCTS and FTS are very similar in clinical features, disease course, predilection site, predilection age, tumor size, and tumor appearance. Imaging examination methods are difficult to distinguish between the two before surgery. The differentiation between the two mainly relies on histopathology and immunohistochemistry, and the two also exhibit different molecular genetics. Although both L-GCTS and FTS are benign tumors, their recurrence rates and other prognostic factors are different. Therefore, it is necessary to clearly distinguish between the two.

title: SOA-UNet: Sparse Otsu-guided Attention U-Net with Adaptive Boundary Loss for Lightweight Brain Tumor Segmentation
abstract: Abstract Accurate segmentation of brain tumors from MRI images is fundamental but computationally intensive due to the tumor region's irregular morphology and heterogeneous intensity. This study presents the SOA-UNet architecture: a lightweight, high-accuracy deep learning model that incorporates sparse feature encoding with Otsu-based attention guidance along with an Adaptive Boundary Loss to achieve accurate localization of tumors with reduced computation. The proposed model utilizes Otsu's thresholding for prior attention, driving the network towards the most critical tumor regions; meanwhile, the sparse encoder removes redundancy and enhances feature discrimination. The newly proposed Adaptive Boundary Loss improves contour delineation while preserving structural integrity along complex tumor boundaries. This study proposes lighweight deep learning model with proper preprocessing that the model can work quickly in terms of training and testing with the dataset. The results position SOA-UNet as the most effective and deployable lightweight framework for reliable brain tumor segmentation, unifying interpretability, accuracy, and speed.

title: Super-Resolution and Artificial Transformer with Attention for accurate detection of brain tumor in MRI-based medical imaging
abstract: Abstract Medical image processing is a vital and rapidly growing field in healthcare and plays a crucial role in diagnosing severe conditions, such as brain tumors. Since brain tumors can be life-threatening, accurate detection through medical imaging is essential. Our research focuses on the accurate detection of brain tumors using deep learning techniques. In most cases, images are highly denoised, irregularly shaped, and either too bright or too dark, which makes accurate detection difficult. So our proposed work enhances significant features in brain images through a super-resolution technique, which improves diagnosis, detection, and up- scales the MRI images. We proposed a novel approach that combines an attention mechanism with an artificial Transformer model. Our model uses channel attention blocks separately to identify the complex features of the image in a channel, and pixel attention enhances the spatial information using a lightweight convolutional layer. This study used a publicly available magnetic resonance imaging dataset containing 7023 images. This work aims to improve the accuracy of tumor detection while maintaining robustness and computational efficiency in real-world scenarios. In addition, we compared our proposed approach with several state-of- the-art deep learning models, including MobileNetV3, DenseNet 121, ResNet 152, VGG 16, and other literature review results for comparative analysis. Our proposed lightweight model significantly enhances diagnostic speed and achieves an impressive precision of 99.16%, outperforming existing techniques.

title: Spectral CT reconstruction algorithm combining total variation and low-rank regularizations based on the Chambolle-Pock method
abstract: Abstract Spectral computed tomography (CT) utilizes photon-counting detectors to acquire multi-energy data for reconstruct images. Due to the limited number of photons in each energy bin, spectral CT imaging suffers from severe quantum noise, making clinical diagnosis more challenging. To address this limitation, we proposed a spectral CT reconstruction model combining total variation (TV) and low-rank regularizations. In the proposed model, the TV regularization was applied to suppress staircase artifacts in spatial domain, while the low-rank regularization was utilized to reduce noise by exploiting the correlation among the spectral CT images in the spectral dimension. To improve the efficiency of the spectral CT reconstruction algorithm, the Chambolle-Pock method was employed to solve our proposed model. Firstly, we constructed the spectral CT reconstruction model combining TV and low-rank regularizations. Secondly, within the Chambolle-Pock optimization framework, the dual variables were introduced to reformulate the reconstruction model as a convex-concave saddle-point problem, which was then transformed into a different equivalent form. Finally, we derived the closed-form solution for each sub-problem in this different equivalent form, thereby obtaining a single-loop iterative reconstruction algorithm. To validate the algorithm’s efficacy, simulated head and thorax phantom data experiments were performed. Extensive experimental results demonstrate the proposed algorithm’s outstanding performance in noise suppression, artifact reduction and detail preservation compared with state-of-the-art methods.

title: Longitudinal Multi-Modality MRI–Ultrasound Cyst-Level Analysis of Polycystic Kidney Disease in a Feline Model: A Proof-of-Concept Study
abstract: Abstract Polycystic kidney disease (PKD) in Persian cats is commonly monitored using total kidney volume (TKV); however, this kidney-level metric does not capture heterogeneity in individual cyst dynamics. Here, a standardized longitudinal imaging framework integrating volumetric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) with serial ultrasound (US) is presented, enabling cyst-level analysis in a feline PKD model followed over two years. MRI-based volumetry quantified individual cyst growth rates and identified structural coalescence events, defined as the persistent loss of visible boundaries between adjacent cysts without implying luminal communication. Serial US provided high-frequency temporal context and supported MRI-defined trends, rather than replacing MRI-based structural assessment. The analysis revealed marked asymmetric progression, with significant enlargement and coalescence of right-sided cysts, while left-sided cysts remained stable. This dual-modality approach demonstrates the feasibility of integrating volumetric MRI with serial ultrasound for longitudinal cyst-level analysis, enabling the identification of asymmetric progression and cyst-level structural remodeling that may be overlooked by kidney-level volumetrics alone. Although based on a single case, this study demonstrates the feasibility of a standardized MRI–ultrasound workflow and provides a methodological framework for future validation in larger cohorts.

title: HLNet: High-Confidence Lightweight Network for Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation
abstract: Abstract Semi-Supervised Learning(SSL) can effectively alleviate the reliance on large amounts of pixel-level labeled data when training fully supervised medical image segmentation models. However, most current semi-supervised learning approaches rely on self-training or consistency regularization methods, which are highly susceptible to erroneous supervision from low-quality pseudo-labels, thus affecting model segmentation performance. Additionally, existing semi-supervised backbone networks typically have large parameter sizes, making them unsuitable for portable device designs. To address these issues, this paper proposes a lightweight semi-supervised segmentation model with high confidence under dual-level perturbations. Perturbations are applied at both the input data and model levels to guide the model in learning more robust feature representations. Furthermore, low-quality pixels are ignored, and EVidence Inference Learning(EVIL) is introduced to estimate the uncertainty of pseudo-labels, mitigating the erroneous supervision from pseudo-labels during training. Experimental results show that the proposed model outperforms comparison models on three different public datasets—ACDC, BUSI, and Promise12. With only 20% labeled data, the model achieves promising segmentation performance in terms of Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) and Jaccard index, while significantly reducing the number of parameters.
